content: Aluminium chlorohydrate is an antiperspirant approved by the FDA for reducing underarm perspiration and decreasing underarm sweating caused by stress. Common adverse reactions include rash and irritation. For adult patients, the FDA-labeled indications include reducing underarm perspiration and stress-induced underarm sweating. There is limited information regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported use of aluminium chlorohydrate in adults. For pediatric patients, there is limited information regarding FDA-labeled use, off-label guideline-supported use, or non-guideline-supported use of aluminium chlorohydrate. Contraindications for aluminium chlorohydrate are not well-documented in the drug label. Warnings include that it is for external use only, is flammable, should not be used on broken skin, and requires consultation with a doctor if the user has kidney disease. Use should be discontinued if rash or irritation occurs. It should be kept out of reach of children, and medical help or contact with a Poison Control Center is advised if accidentally swallowed. Adverse reactions reported in clinical trials and postmarketing experiences are limited. Drug interaction data for aluminium chlorohydrate is also limited. There is no FDA guidance on the use of aluminium chlorohydrate during pregnancy, labor and delivery, or in nursing mothers. Similarly, there is no FDA guidance on its use in pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, or racial populations, nor in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, or in immunocompromised individuals. Aluminium chlorohydrate is administered topically. Information on monitoring, IV compatibility, chronic overdose, pharmacology, mechanism of action, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology is limited in the drug label. Clinical studies and details on how the drug is supplied or stored are not well-documented. Patients are advised to apply the product only to underarms. The interaction between alcohol and aluminium chlorohydrate has not been established, and patients should consult their doctor regarding alcohol use with this medication. The brand name for aluminium chlorohydrate is ANTIPERSPIRANT®. There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names in the drug label.
